Technical Specification and Validation Protocol
Open-Source Candidate Framework for Front-of-Pack Nutrition Labelling in India
Version 2.1  |  August 2026  |  Licence: CC BY 4.0
OPEN SOURCE — CC BY 4.0
Mandatory Disclaimer: AaharAnk v2.1 is a candidate technical specification. Grade thresholds are provisional and require calibration against a representative Indian product dataset of at least 500 products before use in production grading. The AaharAnk grade compares the nutritional composition of eligible packaged foods under the stated methodology. It is not medical advice, does not determine individual dietary suitability, and does not replace the full nutrition and ingredient declaration on the product label. AaharAnk is not a government-approved, validated, or mandated standard.

1. Definitions

TermDefinition
AaharAnk ScoreThe numerical result of subtracting total Positive Points (P) from total Negative Points (N). Lower score = more favourable nutritional composition profile.
AaharAnk GradeOne of five categories (अ, आ, इ, ई, उ) assigned to a product by mapping its AaharAnk Score to provisional grade threshold ranges.
Reference AmountThe basis on which nutritional values are calculated. Default: 100g for solid foods; 100ml for liquid foods. Category 6 uses reference portions (see Section 4.6).
Negative Points (N)Points assigned based on nutrients to be limited: energy, sugars, saturated fat, and sodium.
Positive Points (P)Points assigned based on nutrients and components to be encouraged: dietary fibre, protein, and fruits/vegetables/legumes percentage.
FVL%Estimated percentage by weight of fruit, vegetables, legumes, nuts, and seeds in the product.
Protein Cap RuleInherited from FSA NPM 2004/05: if N ≥ 11 and FVL points < 5, protein points are excluded from P calculation. Exceptions apply (see Section 5.4).
Provisional ThresholdA grade boundary value proposed as a starting point for validation. Not suitable for production use until calibrated against an Indian product dataset.
NABLNational Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (India). Accredited labs required for all testing.
NOVA-4Ultra-processed food as classified by the NOVA system. Not used in the primary score; displayed as a secondary indicator.
NSSNon-sugar sweetener. As defined by WHO 2023 guideline: all synthetic and naturally occurring or modified non-nutritive sweeteners not classified as sugars.1
FSA NPM 2004/05UK Food Standards Agency Nutrient Profiling Model 2004/05 (Rayner, Scarborough, Stockley). The declared baseline model for AaharAnk.2

2. Declared Baseline Model

AaharAnk v2.0 is explicitly derived from the UK Food Standards Agency Nutrient Profiling Model 2004/05, hereafter "FSA NPM 2004/05."

  • Citation: Rayner M, Scarborough P, Stockley L. Nutrient Profiles: Options for definitions for use in relation to food promotion and children's diets. London: Food Standards Agency, 2004.
  • URL: https://www.ndph.ox.ac.uk/food-ncd/files/about/uk-ofcom-nutrient-profile-model.pdf
  • Status: Published academic work in the public domain. Not patented or proprietary.
  • Validation: Independently reviewed by the UK Food Standards Agency (2009) and found "generally scientifically robust and fit for purpose."3 Used as the basis for NutriScore (EU) and UK Ofcom HFSS restrictions. Note: Health Star Rating is based on the Australian/NZ Nutrient Profiling Scoring Criterion, which was influenced by but differs from the FSA NPM 2004/05. The FSA review found the model fit for its specified UK application (food promotion to children) — this finding does not validate AaharAnk or its application in India.

AaharAnk does not claim to be an improvement over the FSA NPM 2004/05. It applies the same core model with declared, documented, and unvalidated modifications for Indian food categories. All departures are listed in Section 3 (Model Change Register).

Note on 2022/26 revised UK model: The UK published the outcome of its 2018 NPM review in January 2026, primarily updating the treatment of free sugars and fibre. AaharAnk v2.1 retains the 2004/05 model baseline, as it is the version most widely cited in peer-reviewed FOPL literature and forms the documented basis of NutriScore. A future version will evaluate alignment with the revised model pending FSSAI guidance on free sugars vs total sugars for Indian labelling.

Every departure from the FSA NPM 2004/05 is declared below. The validation status column uses three values: Aligned with FSA NPM, Partially justified — requires validation, or Unvalidated — requires study.

4. Food Classification System

Before calculating a score, every product must be assigned to exactly one of seven food categories. The category determines which algorithm variant applies. Classification is by primary ingredient by weight (>50% rule).

#CategoryClassification RulesSpecial Algorithm
1General FoodsDefault for all solid foods not classified belowStandard algorithm
2BeveragesLiquids intended for drinking. Exception: plain milk and plant-based drinks where milk/plant base >50% by weight → Category 4Stricter thresholds; only plain water auto-grades अ
3Fats, Oils & GheeFat/oil is primary ingredient (>50%)Sat fat ratio scoring replaces absolute sat fat
4Dairy & PaneerMilk or milk-derived product where milk is primaryProtein always counted (no protein cap applies)
5Nuts, Seeds & Dry FruitsWhole or processed nuts, seeds, dried fruits as primary ingredientSat fat ratio scoring; protein always counted
6Masalas, Spices & CondimentsSpice, spice blend, condiment, pickle, chutney. Typical serving <25g.Evaluated per reference portion, not per 100g
7Millets & Traditional GrainsWhole or minimally processed millet or traditional grain ≥50% by weightMillet bonus +2 P points (eligibility check required)
Multiple-ingredient products: If a product spans two categories, classify by the primary ingredient by weight. If the primary ingredient comprises >50% by weight, its category takes precedence. If no single ingredient exceeds 50%, classify as Category 1 (General Foods) and document the classification rationale.

4.6 Category 6 — Reference Portions (India-Specific)

All reference portions below are provisional research values. Exact documentary citations (specific publication, edition, table and page) for each value are outstanding and must be confirmed at V-05. Until verified, these should be treated as proposed starting points for the pilot study, not established regulatory reference amounts.
Product TypeProposed PortionProposed Source (to be verified)
Ground single spices (haldi, chilli, coriander, cumin, pepper)5gICMR dietary guidelines [exact document, year, page outstanding]
Spice blends (garam masala, sambhar, biryani, pav bhaji masala)10gRecipe-based estimate for 4-serving Indian preparation [not an authoritative source — requires ICMR/Codex validation]
Pickles, achaar (all varieties)15gNational Nutrition Monitoring Bureau [exact survey, year, table outstanding]
Condiments (ketchup, soy sauce, vinegar)15gCodex Alimentarius [exact standard number and table outstanding]
Honey20gFSSAI labelling guidance [exact notification outstanding]
Chutneys (mint, tamarind, coconut)20gRecipe-based estimate [not an authoritative source — requires validation]

Category 6 scoring procedure: Obtain lab-tested nutritional values per 100g. Multiply each nutrient value by (reference portion ÷ 100) to convert to per-portion values. Apply the standard point-allocation tables directly to these per-portion values — do not convert back to per-100g. The scores are thus computed on a per-portion basis, reflecting actual dietary exposure rather than a per-100g analytical equivalent. This is an AaharAnk-specific adaptation and is marked as unvalidated in the Model Change Register.

5. Complete Algorithm

5.1 Core Formula

AaharAnk Score = N − P

Corrected score range: Theoretical minimum −18 (Category 7 product with all bonuses, P=18, N=0). Theoretical maximum +40 (maximum N=40, P=0). No operational range is stated — no Indian product dataset has been analysed to establish one.

Maximum protein = 5 pts (FSA NPM 2004/05). Subject to protein cap rule (Section 5.4).

G. Fruits, Vegetables, Legumes, Nuts & Seeds (FVL) — % by weight

Declared modification from FSA NPM 2004/05: The original FSA model awards FVL points at only four levels: 0 (≤40%), 1 (>40%), 2 (>60%), 5 (>80%). AaharAnk v2.1 retains these four levels exactly. The intermediate 3-pt and 4-pt bands in v2.0 were an error and have been removed.
0 pts1 pt2 pts5 pts
≤40%>40% to ≤60%>60% to ≤80%>80%

Note: FVL% includes fruit, vegetables, nuts, and legumes as defined in FSA NPM 2004/05. Legumes and seeds are included in AaharAnk as a declared extension of the qualifying ingredients list (see Model Change Register row 10).

H. Millet Bonus (Category 7 only)

Add +2 P points if ALL of the following are true:

  • Product classified as Category 7 (Millets & Traditional Grains)
  • Whole millet content ≥50% by weight (declared on label or verified by ingredient list)
  • Fibre score (Table E) ≥ 2 points
  • Product is NOT classified NOVA-4

I. Fermented Food Bonus

Add +1 P point if ALL of the following are true:

  • Product is plain dahi/yogurt with live cultures declared on label at end of shelf life, OR traditional brine-fermented pickle (not vinegar/acetic acid-based)
  • No added sugar or sweetener
  • Not flavoured or modified with additional ingredients
Maximum P = Fibre(5) + Protein(5) + FVL(5) + Millet Bonus(2, if eligible) + Fermented(1, if eligible) = 18 pts maximum (Category 7 eligible product)

5.4 Protein Cap Rule (inherited from FSA NPM 2004/05)

Condition: If calculated N ≥ 11 AND FVL points < 5

Then: Protein points are excluded from P total

Formula becomes: P = Fibre + FVL (protein excluded)

Exceptions — protein always counted regardless:

  • Category 4 (Dairy & Paneer)
  • Category 5 (Nuts, Seeds & Dry Fruits)
Rationale: The protein cap prevents products high in sugar, fat, or sodium from achieving a more favourable grade simply by adding protein. Exceptions for dairy and nuts reflect that protein is a defining nutritional characteristic of these categories and excluding it would produce misleading comparisons within the category.

6. Secondary Indicators

Secondary indicators appear alongside the AaharAnk badge but are not incorporated into the grade score.

IndicatorTriggerDisplay TextScientific Basis
NSS Disclosure Any NSS present in ingredient list (acesulfame K, aspartame, sucralose, stevia/steviol glycosides, saccharin, neotame, advantame, cyclamates) "Contains Non-Sugar Sweetener" WHO's 2023 conditional recommendation advises against using NSS as a means of achieving weight control or reducing NCD risk.1 The recommendation does not apply to individuals with pre-existing diabetes. The proposed disclosure format itself remains unvalidated as a FOPL tool.
High Processing Classification under a validated NOVA decision protocol applied to the full ingredient list. Note: the "High Processing" indicator is not operational until a validated Indian-specific NOVA decision tree is published. The ingredient examples listed here (hydrogenated oils, modified starches, etc.) are illustrative of NOVA-4 markers, not a definitive classification rule. A single listed ingredient does not automatically trigger classification. "High Processing" NOVA processing level is associated with adverse dietary patterns. Displayed separately because NOVA classification inter-rater reliability requires a validated Indian decision tree before incorporation into the primary score.

7. Pseudocode

The following pseudocode is provided so that two independent assessors applying the same lab data should reach an identical AaharAnk Score. Any implementation must produce identical results for all worked examples in Section 8.

FUNCTION calculate_aaharank_v21(product):

  // STEP 1: Classify product into one of 7 categories
  category = classify_category(product)

  // STEP 2: Determine reference amount
  IF category == 6:
    ref_amount = get_reference_portion(product.type)
    // Convert to per-100g equivalent before scoring
    scale = ref_amount / 100
    energy = product.energy_kj * scale
    sugars = product.total_sugars_g * scale
    sat_fat = product.sat_fat_g * scale
    sodium = product.sodium_mg * scale
    fibre = product.fibre_g * scale
    protein = product.protein_g * scale
  ELSE:
    // Use per-100g or per-100ml values as supplied by NABL lab
    energy = product.energy_kj_per_100
    sugars = product.total_sugars_g_per_100
    sat_fat = product.sat_fat_g_per_100
    sodium = product.sodium_mg_per_100
    fibre = product.fibre_g_per_100
    protein = product.protein_g_per_100

  fvl_pct = product.fvl_percent

  // STEP 3: Calculate Negative Points
  N_energy = lookup_energy_pts(energy)        // Table A
  N_sugars = lookup_sugars_pts(sugars)        // Table B

  IF category IN [3, 5]:
    IF product.total_fat_g > 0:
      sfr = (sat_fat / product.total_fat_g) * 100
    ELSE:
      sfr = 0
    N_satfat = lookup_sfr_pts(sfr)            // Table C2
  ELSE:
    N_satfat = lookup_satfat_pts(sat_fat)     // Table C

  N_sodium = lookup_sodium_pts(sodium)        // Table D

  N = N_energy + N_sugars + N_satfat + N_sodium
  // No sweetener penalty in primary score
  // No NOVA penalty in primary score

  // STEP 4: Calculate Positive Points
  P_fibre = lookup_fibre_pts(fibre)           // Table E
  P_protein = lookup_protein_pts(protein)     // Table F
  P_fvl = lookup_fvl_pts(fvl_pct)            // Table G

  // STEP 5: Apply Protein Cap Rule (inherited from FSA NPM 2004/05)
  IF N >= 11 AND P_fvl < 5:
    IF category NOT IN [4, 5]:               // Cat 4, 5 exempt
      P_protein = 0                          // Exclude protein

  // STEP 6: Apply India-specific bonuses
  P_millet = 0
  IF category == 7:
    IF (product.whole_millet_pct >= 50 AND
        P_fibre >= 2 AND
        product.nova_group != 4):
      P_millet = 2

  P_fermented = 0
  IF (product.type IN ["plain_dahi", "brine_pickle"] AND
      product.live_cultures == TRUE AND
      product.added_sugar == FALSE AND
      product.flavoured == FALSE):
    P_fermented = 1

  P = P_fibre + P_protein + P_fvl + P_millet + P_fermented

  // STEP 7: Calculate final score
  score = N - P

  // STEP 8: Map score to grade (provisional thresholds)
  grade = lookup_grade(score, category)

  // STEP 9: Determine secondary indicators
  nss_flag = any_nss_in_ingredients(product.ingredients)
  nova_flag = (product.nova_group == 4)

  RETURN {
    score: score,
    N: N,
    P: P,
    grade: grade,
    nss_disclosure: nss_flag,
    high_processing: nova_flag
  }

8. Worked Calculation Examples

Important: All product examples below are illustrative only. The nutritional values used are representative estimates, not lab-tested figures. For the pilot phase, grades may be computed from verified manufacturer-declared nutrition data (as legally required under FSSAI Labelling Regulations 2020), supplemented by NABL-accredited laboratory testing for a representative audit sample. Full NABL testing for all products is recommended before any production-scale grading or mandatory labelling scheme. These examples demonstrate the calculation procedure, not production grades.

8.1 Illustrative Example: Whole Wheat Atta (1 kg)

Category 1 (General Foods). Values per 100g — illustrative only.
Energy: 1420 kJ → 4 ptsSugars: 2.0g → 0 ptsSat Fat: 0.5g → 0 ptsSodium: 5mg → 0 pts

N = 4 + 0 + 0 + 0 = 4

Fibre: 9.0g → 5 pts | Protein: 12.0g → 5 pts (capped at FSA NPM max) | FVL%: 0% → 0 pts

Protein cap check: N(4) < 11 → protein counted. P = 5 + 5 + 0 = 10

Score = 4 − 10 = −6 → Provisional Grade: अ (Higher Quality) [≤0]

8.2 Illustrative Example: Potato Chips (150g)

Category 1 (General Foods) + NOVA-4 flag. Values per 100g — illustrative only.
Energy: 2230 kJ → 7 ptsSugars: 1.2g → 0 ptsSat Fat: 4.5g → 4 ptsSodium: 480mg → 5 pts

N = 7 + 0 + 4 + 5 = 16

Fibre: 3.8g → 1 pt | Protein: 6.0g → 3 pts (pre-cap) | FVL%: 55% → 1 pt (>40% to ≤60% = 1 pt under corrected FSA NPM table)

Protein cap check: N(16) ≥ 11 AND FVL pts(1) < 5 → protein excluded

P = 1 + 0 + 1 = 2

Score = 16 − 2 = 14 → Provisional Grade: ई (Lower Nutritional Quality) [12–20]

Secondary indicators: High Processing flag (NOVA-4).

8.3 Illustrative Example: Garam Masala (100g) — Per-Portion Method

Category 6 (Masalas). Evaluated per 10g reference portion. Values per 100g from lab — illustrative only.

Per 100g lab values: Energy 1340 kJ | Sugars 3.2g | Sat Fat 1.8g | Sodium 520mg | Fibre 14.9g | Protein 12.6g | FVL 100%

Scale to 10g portion (multiply by 10/100 = 0.1): Energy 134 kJ | Sugars 0.32g | Sat Fat 0.18g | Sodium 52mg | Fibre 1.49g | Protein 1.26g

N = 0 + 0 + 0 + 0 = 0

Fibre: 1.49g → 0 pts | Protein: 1.26g → 0 pts | FVL%: 100% → 5 pts

Protein cap: N(0) < 11 → protein counted. P = 0 + 0 + 5 = 5

Score = 0 − 5 = −5 → Provisional Grade: अ (Higher Quality) [≤0]
Important limitation: Per-portion scoring for Category 6 products can produce near-zero negative scores for highly concentrated foods (e.g., high-sodium pickle pastes, seasoning mixes) that may contribute meaningfully to daily sodium intake across multiple servings. This is a known limitation of reference-portion scoring. The sodium contribution of condiments and spices should be assessed cumulatively. The Category 6 method remains unvalidated and subject to revision after V-05.

8.4 Illustrative Example: Pure Cow Ghee (500ml)

Category 3 (Fats, Oils & Ghee). Sat fat ratio scoring. Values per 100g — illustrative only.

Total Fat: 99.5g | Sat Fat: 61.9g | SFR = (61.9/99.5) × 100 = 62.2% → 10 pts

Energy: 3696 kJ → 10 pts | Sugars: 0g → 0 pts | Sodium: 2mg → 0 pts

N = 10 + 0 + 10 + 0 = 20

Fibre: 0g → 0 pts | Protein: 0.3g → 0 pts | FVL%: 0% → 0 pts

P = 0

Score = 20 − 0 = 20 → Provisional Grade: ई (Lower Nutritional Quality) [12–20]
Threshold boundary note: Score of 20 falls within ई (12–20) under provisional thresholds. This illustrates how the boundary between ई and उ will require careful calibration — ghee sits close to that boundary and small threshold adjustments could shift it. Until threshold validation is complete, this illustrative grade should be treated as approximate.

10. Validation Protocol

The following ten gates must be completed before AaharAnk v2.1 thresholds are confirmed and before any production-grade labelling commences.

GateRequirementStandardOwner
V-01Mathematical proof: verify score range and threshold coverage with no gapsComputer-verified calculation across all threshold boundary valuesTechnical Secretariat
V-02Algorithm reproducibility: two independent assessors reach identical score for same lab dataZero discrepancy across 20 test productsScientific Advisory Council
V-03Dataset calibration: compute scores for ≥500 representative Indian products across all 7 categoriesRepresentative sample validated by food scientist. Dataset published openly.Scientific Advisory Council
V-04Threshold review: assess whether provisional thresholds correctly classify products across all categoriesPeer review by minimum 2 independent food scientistsScientific Advisory Council
V-05Indian food category validation: confirm Category 6 reference portions and Category 7 millet eligibility criteria against real productsComparison against ICMR and Codex reference dataNutrient Profiling Working Group
V-06Consumer comprehension study: ≥400 respondents across literacy levels, regions, and languagesPublished study report. ≥70% correct identification of अ as most favourable, उ as least favourableConsumer Testing Working Group
V-07Legal IP review: confirm CC BY 4.0 application, trademark approach, and open-source model are legally sound under Indian IP lawWritten opinion from qualified Indian IP counselLegal Counsel
V-08FSSAI alignment check: confirm AaharAnk methodology is compatible with existing FSSAI Food Safety and Standards (Labelling and Display) Regulations 2020Written assessment by food regulatory lawyerLegal Counsel
V-09Conflict-of-interest audit: all SAC members declare funding sourcesPublished declarations on public repositoryCOI Committee

11. Open Governance

  • Methodology licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (CC BY 4.0). https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/
  • Name and badge design: Trademark protection (pending filing) to ensure accurate use. No licensing fee for compliant use. Modified versions must use a different name and badge design.
  • Version control: Every published version carries a version number and SHA-256 checksum of the specification document. Users must declare which version they applied.
  • Public repository: Methodology, point tables, pseudocode, dataset, worked examples, and SAC minutes published at a public URL with version control. URL to be confirmed at v2.0 final release.
  • Update cycle: Annual review by Scientific Advisory Council. Minor updates (threshold adjustments): 30-day public comment, 90-day regrade period. Major updates (algorithm changes): 90-day public comment, 180-day transition.
  • Conflict of interest: Industry funding must be declared by all SAC members. Industry representatives may participate as observers, not voting members.

13. Limitations and Unresolved Questions

  1. Grade thresholds are provisional: The thresholds in Section 9 have not been calibrated against Indian product data. They may need significant adjustment after V-03.
  2. Sat fat ratio scoring (Categories 3, 5): Not validated. The boundary values in Table C2 are proposed based on general knowledge of Indian oil fatty acid profiles, not a systematic study.
  3. Millet and fermented food bonuses: Not validated. Both are based on general nutritional science reasoning. The specific bonus magnitudes (+2, +1) are arbitrary pending validation.
  4. FVL% estimation: The calculation method for FVL% in composite and processed foods is not fully specified in this version. A supplementary FVL calculation guide will be published before V-05.
  5. NOVA classification decision tree: No India-specific NOVA-4 decision tree exists. Inter-rater reliability of NOVA classification for Indian foods is unestablished. The "High Processing" secondary indicator should be interpreted cautiously until this is resolved.
  6. Free sugars vs total sugars: AaharAnk v2.0 uses total sugars (aligned with FSA NPM 2004/05). The 2022 UK review moved to free sugars. FSSAI guidance on which sugar measurement to use for Indian FOPL will determine whether AaharAnk needs to align in a future version.
  7. Category-specific thresholds: Only general food thresholds are specified in v2.0. Category-specific thresholds for beverages, fats/oils, dairy, and other categories require dedicated validation studies.
  8. Devanagari literacy: Consumer comprehension across literacy levels, regions, and non-Hindi-speaking populations is unestablished. V-06 (comprehension study) is mandatory before making any claim about pan-Indian applicability.
